newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Analysts say NorScan stock fall as expected.
newsitem.headline: Analysts say NorScan stock fall as expected.

text.p: Stock levels of North American and Scandinavian (NorScan) pulp producers in June were in line with expectations and not likely to drive pulp prices or forestry shares up, analysts said on Tuesday.
"The figures confirm the market situation. It is ticking slowly away. It's going in the right direction," said Skandiabanken analyst Andreas Nyberg.
He said the stock levels were not likely to change the prices of forestry shares, which have risen lately.
The forestry sector index on the Stockholm bourse was 0.66 percent lower at 1200 GMT while the Stockholm general index fell 0.5 percent.
Finnish news agency STT quoted Finnish Forest Industries Federation as saying Norscan stocks fell by 60,000 tonnes to just under 1.6 million tonnes in June.
At the start of the year NorScan stocks stood at more than two million tonnes, according to the Finnish industry organisation, but fell due to halts in production and with stronger demand.
Analysts said stocks were getting close to the important level of 1.5 million tonnes, a level which is often considered to trigger price rises.
But analysts said prices had already started to climb so the June changes were not so market sensitive.
"It was a slightly smaller fall than usual (for June) but I do not think this was a surprise," said another analyst.

One analyst said the falling stocks, together with the stronger dollar, were positive for Swedish and Finnish forestry companies, most of whom had managed to get above the break-even level of around $600 a tonne.
